title: OpenAI Slashes API Prices for GPT-5.6 Lineup As Efficiency Gains Pay Off
key_facts: OpenAI announced cost reductions and performance upgrades across its GPT-5.6 model family 'on Thursday'; the rate cuts start July 30 (30 Jul 2026 was a Thursday).
API rates for GPT-5.6 Luna were cut by 80% and for GPT-5.6 Terra by 20%.
New rates: Luna $0.20 per million input tokens and $1.20 per million output tokens; Terra $2 and $12.
OpenAI also debuted a 'Fast mode' for the flagship GPT-5.6 Sol, designed to process high-priority enterprise workloads up to 2.5 times faster than standard speeds.
The cuts extend to paid corporate accounts including ChatGPT Work and Codex, where Luna and Terra use fewer quota credits without changing subscription tiers.
OpenAI attributes the savings to optimisation across its software stack: improved hardware routing, production inference software and smarter context caching.

OpenAI says that in human-supervised testing GPT-5.6 Sol rewrote critical production software kernels, cutting end-to-end serving overhead by 20 percent, and improved token-generation efficiency by more than 15 percent in automated experiments.
quote_evidence: Starting July 30, the artificial intelligence research laboratory reduced API rates for GPT-5.6 Luna by 80% and GPT-5.6 Terra by 20%.
Pricing for GPT-5.6 Terra has been set to $2 per million input tokens and $12 per million output tokens.
The company said it is passing the reduced operational costs directly to developers, enterprise subscribers, and cloud platform partners like Amazon Web Services (AWS).
why_it_matters_hint: Developers and companies using OpenAI's smaller models paid much less per use from 30 Jul 2026.
event_date: 30 Jul 2026 (OpenAI's own post and Yahoo Finance's copy of this Stocktwits piece are dated Thu 30 Jul 2026 in Google News).
